task.title: Authentication, BYOK Flow, and Future Google OAuth Requirements
task.objective: Refine the authentication onboarding flow, improve UX around API key collection, and prepare for future Google OAuth integration without implementing it yet.

requirement.description:
Remove the current behavior that immediately redirects users to the BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) page after login.
Instead:
1. User logs in successfully. 2. User enters the main application directly. 3. During the user's first search or first action that requires an API key, check whether a valid key already exists. 4. Only if no key is present should the BYOK screen/modal appear. 5. After the key is provided, continue the original search automatically.

acceptance-criteria.item: No forced BYOK screen immediately after login.
Main application is accessible immediately after authentication.
BYOK appears only when actually required.
Original user action resumes after key submission.

requirement.description:
Ensure email verification works correctly after deployment.
Current concern: verification links may behave as if they are tied to the device that initiated signup.
Expected behavior after deployment: a user should be able to open the verification email from any device, browser, or operating system and successfully verify their account.
Verification must be domain-based and session-safe rather than tied to the original signup device.

acceptance-criteria.item: No dependency on the originating device.
Works correctly when deployed to DigitalOcean.

requirement.description:
Google OAuth authentication is planned but should NOT be implemented in this iteration.
For now: - Document all integration requirements. - Identify required Google Cloud Console configuration. - Identify required redirect URIs. - Identify required Supabase OAuth settings. - Create a clear implementation checklist.
Implementation should be deferred until after deployment.

acceptance-criteria.item: No Google OAuth code merged yet.
All required configuration values clearly listed.

requirement.description:
Review the provided Google OAuth configuration screenshot and determine exactly which values are required from me.
Present the required fields in a copy-paste-friendly checklist so I can provide the information quickly.

deliverables.item: List of required Google OAuth configuration values.

engineering-principles.item: Design for future scalability and OAuth expansion.
